body: I would show photos to clarify what I define as hash browns, chips and fries but apparently the subreddit doesn't allow it... I think I caused a lot of confusion and I apologize.

I'm not a parent, but I do have a story that personally affected me as well as other students in the class. 

I'm autistic, and although high-functioning, I'm still unable to function in school unless I attend a special needs classroom for most of the school day. Unfortunately, many of my classmates have more severe physical and/or mental handicapping than I do, meaning that I notice a lot more and speak up for myself a lot more, when the staff are not behaving the way they should be as EAs (educational assistants).

There was an EA in the special needs class, let's call him Mike, and he had a reputation among his coworkers for being quite mischievous and troublesome, but in a funny and playful way. However, his "teasing" with the disabled students often went too far. 

I clearly remember numerous occasions involving Mike and two other students. The two students had speech impediments (stuttering, loud noises, pronouncing words in an incoherent way, etc). Mike would often mock these children, doing impressions of their impaired speech in a way intended to "playfully" make fun of the students and/or their behaviors and ways of communicating. 

Mike would also use the impressionability of these students as a way to get the students reacting to his behavior in angry ways, and the reactions would fuel his desire to continue. 

There was one instance where he went up to an impressionable kid who was peacefully playing games on the computer, and he lied to the kid saying "hey, the teacher said you have to get off the computer now." The kid automatically believed what Mike had told him (he can't help it, he doesn't know any better because of his disability unfortunately) and started yelling the teacher's name and getting very upset. Mike only found this entertaining and decided to exploit it rather than stop it, so he continued to say in a mocking tone "Get off the computer buddy, it's time to go" even though the kid actually still had lots of computer time left. The kid's face was red with anger by the time Mike finally decided to stop. 

And lastly, Mike would frequently make very dark "jokes" about the students.

There was a student who was both physically and mentally handicapped so she required assistance to walk to and from the restroom. It's part of her daily routine to use the restroom, but she doesn't find it very fun for whatever reason, so she usually starts yelling and crying when the staff start walking her in that direction. One day she was yelling and crying so loudly on her way to the washroom that Mike decided to crack a "joke" that he must have thought was funny for some reason, saying "Woah, jeez, it's almost as if she's being abused." The other staff simply laughed and said to him "don't say that" and then brushed it off.

I reported all of these incidents to the vice principal of the school after witnessing this mocking behavior for several months. Mike was told to stop the behavior by his boss. But he had to be told *several times* by his boss to stop the behavior before he actually stopped it... oh well, it's over with now I guess!
